List the pathways with the most certain next state

Source: R/pathways.R
sharp_pathways.Rd

sharp_pathways() returns the pathways whose most likely next state has the highest probability. A pathway with a next-state probability close to 1 is followed almost always by the same state, a near-deterministic step in the process; a probability close to \(1/k\) (\(k\) states) means the next state is hard to predict from that history. Sharp pathways with small counts are often artefacts of few observations; set min_count accordingly.

Usage

sharp_pathways(tree, top = 10L, min_count = 1L)

Arguments

tree

A transitiontrees object.

top

Number of pathways to return. Default 10.

min_count

Keep pathways that occurred at least this many times. Default 1.

Value

A data.frame with the columns of tree_pathways(), one row per pathway, sorted by next_probability in decreasing order, at most top rows.

Conditions

transitiontrees_bad_input when tree is not a fitted tree.

See also

tree_pathways(), common_pathways(), tree_dependence() for the entropy of each prediction.

Examples

tree <- context_tree(trajectories, max_depth = 3)
sharp_pathways(tree, top = 5, min_count = 20)
#>                                  pathway depth count likely_next
#> 1             Active -> Active -> Active     3   316      Active
#> 2                       Active -> Active     2   433      Active
#> 3          Average -> Average -> Average     3   248     Average
#> 4    Disengaged -> Disengaged -> Average     3    31     Average
#> 5 Disengaged -> Disengaged -> Disengaged     3    81  Disengaged
#>   next_probability  divergence changes_prediction
#> 1        0.8354430 0.011491875              FALSE
#> 2        0.7852194 0.028601567              FALSE
#> 3        0.7177419 0.006242261              FALSE
#> 4        0.7085484 0.198404690              FALSE
#> 5        0.7037037 0.008106021              FALSE
